ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a circle with F as the center, and A, B, C, D are on the circle. Line segment AC passes through the center F, indicating that AC is a diameter, so A, F, C are collinear, and ∠AFC is a straight angle. In the figure, radii are drawn from F to B, C, D, A respectively; ∠BFC is labeled 72°, ∠CFD is labeled (4a−1)°, and ∠AFD is labeled (2a−5)°. Reasoning: Because AC is a diameter, the semicircle from FC to FA corresponds to 180°. This semicircle is divided into two parts by ∠CFD and ∠DFA, therefore (4a−1)+(2a−5)=180. Combining gives 6a−6=180, so 6a=186, a=31. Thus ∠CFD=4a−1=4(31)−1=123°. The larger angle from D to B passing through C is ∠DFC+∠CFB=123°+72°=195°, so the smaller ∠DFB=360°−195°=165°.

raw_record.question_text: Find the measure of $\angle DFB$ on $\odot F$ with diameter $\overline{AC}$.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: F is the center of the circle, A and C lie opposite each other on a straight line through F, so AC is a diameter. The central angle between FB and FC is labeled 72°, the central angle between FC and FD is labeled (4a−1)°, and the central angle between FA and FD is labeled (2a−5)°. From the text, use that the circle is ⊙F with diameter AC, confirming A, F, C are collinear and ∠AFC is a straight angle. Set (2a−5)+(4a−1)=180 to solve for a. Then compute ∠CFD=4a−1 and use the full circle or the adjacent central angles: the reflex path from D to B through C is ∠DFC+∠CFB, so the desired smaller ∠DFB is 360−[(4a−1)+72]. This gives 165°.
